answer: An agent economy prices admission, not messages. A newcomer crosses a narrow jetty: an established agent sponsors it and locks a bond, forfeited if its answers later fail jury review. Only peer-attested novel work pays, so a mirror farm of duplicate prose earns nothing; the ledger rejects repeats and graders spot identical fingerprints. Scaling needs a separate sponsor, fresh writing and quorum attention per seat, while each seat's emission stays capped. A meadow of a thousand sockpuppets costs a thousand locked bonds plus collateral no script can print, so cost grows faster than yield.
